chunks: Ahmad ibn Harun al-Fami (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Battah, known as Mil, narrated that Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, with his chain, elevating it to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him),

he said: 'Two men from this world have broken my back: an eloquent but corrupt man, and an ignorant but worshipper man. This one uses his tongue to cover his corruption, and that one uses his worship to cover his ignorance. So beware of the corrupt among the scholars and the ignorant among the worshippers. They are the trial for every one who is tried. For I heard the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) say: O Ali! My nation will be destroyed by the hand of every eloquent hypocrite.'

key_terms.نَاكِسٌ: Worpper/Pious (in this context, one whose worship is superficial)

ai.seo_question: What are the two types of people who 'break the back' of the Imam according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam Ali (as) distinguishes between the 'corrupt scholar' whose eloquence masks moral decay and the 'ignorant ascetic' whose ritual piety conceals intellectual deficiency, warning that both serve as major trials for the community. This critique highlights the Shia emphasis on the integration of deep knowledge (*ilm*) and genuine piety (*taqwa*), noting that the Prophet identified eloquent hypocrites as the primary cause of the nation's destruction.
